methods.rationale: Capacity cross-check: Q4 2025 owned H100-equivalent compute is grown to Q3 2026, multiplied by the direct-API compute share, utilization and throughput. It is structurally independent of the recent token/min trend but depends on four broad assumptions. Failure modes: total owned compute includes training/internal/consumer uses, H100-equivalent throughput is highly model-mix dependent, and the direct-API share is not directly disclosed.

assumptions.name: Q3 2026/Q2 2026 growth factor for Gemini direct API tokens per minute
assumptions.rationale: Set below the 60% QoQ growth reported for Q1 2026 (p86) to reflect deceleration as the base grows, but not all the way to flat because Gemini 4 launches, price cuts and agentic API features likely supported Q3 usage. p1 and p19 provide the observed Q1-to-Q2 level change.
assumptions.applies_when: Q3 2026 direct-API token volume follows a continuation of the recent growth trajectory with modest deceleration from the prior quarter.
assumptions.falsified_by: Alphabet or credible pre-release evidence indicating Q3 2026 direct API tokens/min below about 22B (no growth) or above about 40B (reacceleration), or a disclosed QoQ growth rate outside the assumed range.

assumptions.name: average inference throughput per H100-equivalent serving Gemini models
assumptions.rationale: A blended H100-equivalent inference throughput for a mix of large Gemini Pro-class and smaller Flash-class models, with batching. Larger models run below this and lighter models above it; the wide range reflects model-mix and serving-efficiency uncertainty.
assumptions.applies_when: Used only in the capacity decomposition where total owned H100-equivalent compute is multiplied by direct-API share and utilization.
assumptions.falsified_by: Benchmarks showing Gemini production inference throughput per TPU/GPU is consistently far outside this range, or evidence that most direct API traffic is served on non-H100-equivalent custom silicon with radically different effective throughput.

assumptions.name: average utilization of direct-API inference accelerators
assumptions.rationale: Large API platforms typically run high average utilization but reserve headroom for burstiness, rate limits and failover. A 50-90% band is realistic for inference capacity that is actively serving external API traffic.
assumptions.applies_when: Applied to the share of total owned compute allocated to direct API inference in m3.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence of sustained very low utilization or severe capacity constraints causing widespread Gemini API throttling in Q3 2026.

assumptions.name: share of total Alphabet owned H100-equivalent compute allocated to direct API inference
assumptions.rationale: Direct API customers are only one use of Alphabet's owned compute, alongside training, internal serving, Search/AI Overviews, Gemini app and Cloud-hosted third-party workloads. The Q2 2026 22B/min anchor implies a low-single-digit share under plausible throughput assumptions, so 5% is a central value with wide uncertainty.
assumptions.applies_when: Used in m3 to bridge total owned compute to compute serving external Gemini API/Vertex direct API customers.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that external direct API traffic consumes a much larger or much smaller fraction of Alphabet inference compute, for example from disclosed TPU allocation or severe API capacity constraints.

assumptions.name: growth factor in total owned H100-equivalent capacity from Q4 2025 to Q3 2026
assumptions.rationale: Alphabet's H1 2026 capex (p55) and Q2 2026 capex (p58), including a large server share (p59), imply rapid compute expansion after Q4 2025. A 1.5x central capacity growth from Q4 2025 to Q3 2026 is plausible, with uncertainty around commissioning lags and how much capex becomes owned H100-equivalent capacity.
assumptions.applies_when: Used to move the Q4 2025 owned-capacity estimate p60/p61 forward to the Q3 2026 target period.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence of much slower or much faster TPU/GPU commissioning, or a disclosed Q3 2026 owned compute capacity far outside 1.2x-2.0x the Q4 2025 estimate.

Monthly tokens across all Google surfaces include consumer, internal, Search/AI Mode, and other workloads. They are not the direct-API customer run-rate and cannot be converted without a surface-share bridge.

Google Cloud revenue, growth, and backlog are broad Cloud metrics including infrastructure and other products, not Gemini direct-API token volume. They indicate demand strength but cannot be used as a direct token level.

Alphabet capex: Q1 2026 $35.7B plus Q2 2026 $44.9B is consistent with H1 2026 $80.6B; Q2 capex split roughly 60% servers. This supports inference-capacity growth assumptions, not a direct token level.

Epoch AI Q4 2025 owned compute: TPU-only 3.1M-4.5M H100-equivalents (midpoint 3.8M), with Nvidia GPUs implied at roughly 1M. They come from the same estimate and are not independent. They require a capacity-growth adjustment to Q3 2026 for the capacity route.

OpenAI API token usage is a different company but a useful growth analogue: 6B/min October 2025 to 15B/min March 2026, roughly 2.5x in five months. Gemini's Q2 2026 22B/min is already above the March 2026 OpenAI level, so this constrains direction, not Gemini's level.

Gemini 4 Argon list prices of $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens are relevant to any revenue-to-token conversion, but a conversion requires unknown output-token mix, discounts, and free-tier share. Not a direct volume observation.

SDK download counts show developer attention: google-genai 216.7M PyPI and @google/genai 45.8M npm versus openai 295.9M PyPI and anthropic 119.8M PyPI. Gemini's lower SDK downloads than OpenAI coexist with higher disclosed token/min, so downloads are not proportional to token volume; direction/context only.

Customer token thresholds imply large absolute usage but are far below the reported aggregate: 330 customers each >1T tokens/year and 35 each >10T/year imply roughly 350T tokens/year from those customers (~0.7B/min), versus 22B/min total. They are non-binding lower bounds.

The quoted 52x growth from ~8.3T tokens/month to an 'annualized run rate' of >430T is internally inconsistent: 52x of 8.3T/month is ~432T/month, while 430T/year is ~35.8T/month. Neither reconciles cleanly with 10B/min (~5,256T/year) or 22B/min. Scope/arithmetic is unusable.

assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that Q3 2026 QoQ growth was below 10% or above 55%, or that a major Gemini API launch/price cut caused a step change within Q3 2026.

assumptions.name: average inference throughput per H100-equivalent serving Gemini models
assumptions.rationale: An H100-equivalent accelerator running batched LLM inference can produce thousands of output tokens per second for smaller/faster models, but much less for large Gemini Pro-class models. The 2,000 token/s central value is a blended throughput across Flash/Pro serving, with a wide range for model mix, batching, and speculative decoding.
assumptions.applies_when: Capacity is expressed in H100-equivalents and used for a blended Gemini serving mix rather than one specific model.
assumptions.falsified_by: Gemini inference benchmarks or capacity disclosures showing sustained throughput outside roughly 800-5,000 tokens/s per H100-equivalent.

assumptions.name: average utilization of direct-API inference accelerators
assumptions.rationale: Production inference fleets usually run at high average utilization because of batching and continuous serving, but need headroom for bursts, failover, and regional demand. A 70% average utilization over a quarter is plausible for a large managed API.
assumptions.applies_when: The capacity route estimates average quarter-level output from installed inference capacity rather than peak capacity.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that direct-API inference utilization is consistently below 50% or above 90% over the quarter.

assumptions.name: share of total Alphabet owned H100-equivalent compute allocated to direct API inference
assumptions.rationale: Alphabet's owned compute serves Search/AI Mode, the Gemini app, Workspace, internal workloads, Cloud training, and many other serving uses. Direct API is one channel, so only a minority of H100-equivalent capacity should be assigned to it. The 5% central share allows for substantial direct-API serving while leaving most capacity for other uses.
assumptions.applies_when: p60 and p61 represent total owned Alphabet compute, including training and all serving surfaces, not dedicated Gemini API capacity.
assumptions.falsified_by: Disclosure or credible estimate that direct-API inference uses more than ~12% or less than ~2% of total Alphabet owned H100-equivalent capacity.

assumptions.name: growth factor in total owned H100-equivalent capacity from Q4 2025 to Q3 2026
assumptions.rationale: Alphabet spent about $80.6B on capex in H1 2026 after large Q1 and Q2 outlays, with roughly 60% of Q2 capex going to servers. Three quarters of deployment should raise owned H100-equivalent capacity meaningfully, but not all capex adds inference capacity and TPU/GPU shipments have lead times. A 1.5x central growth factor over three quarters is reasonable, with a 1.2x-2.0x range.
assumptions.applies_when: p60/p61 are Q4 2025 owned-capacity estimates and Q3 2026 capacity is approximated by applying a three-quarter growth factor.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that Alphabet's owned H100-equivalent capacity grew less than 20% or more than 100% between Q4 2025 and Q3 2026.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
